To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electrical properties of rat pancreatic acinar cells were studied by the whole cell tight-seal recording technique.

1) in the absence of secretagogues, the main conductances in pancreatic acinar cell are Cl and K; 2) the activation of a cationic conductance, selective for Ca2+, Na+ and H+ is induced by internal calcium; 3) acetylcholine and CCK activate a Ca conductance which in turn activates Cl and cation conductances; 4) the secretagogue-induced conductances are increased by depolarisation; 5)
the acinar cell membrane is a Cl-selective membrane and that acetylcholine, cholecystokin, and secretin activate a Cl conductance by increasing the intracellular concentration of calcium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electrical properties of pancreatic acinar cells.
the electrical properties of single pancreatic acinar cells and the effect of secretagogues and calcium on these properties.
the electrical properties of pancreatic acinar cells isolated in culture.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electrical characteristics of the pancreatic acinar cells are very similar to the characteristics of other epithelial cells.
, in the rat exocrine pancrea, the electrical properties of acinar cells are similar to those of other exocrine glands, but the secretagogue-induced conductances are different.
the secretagogue-induced increase in permeability is not due to the activation of K channels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, under resting conditions, the acinar cell is characterised by the presence of a large Cl conductance, a low permeability to K and the absence of K channels sensitive to intracellular Ca.
, in pancreatic cells, the Ca and secretagogues induced Cl and cation conductances are not voltage-dependent.

, in rat pancreatic acinar cells: 1) a Ca-dependent Cl conductance is present; 2) an internal Ca-dependent, voltage-independent, cationic conductance is present and is the major conductance activated by high internal Ca; 3) acetylcholine and CCK increase the internal Ca and activate either only a Cl or both Cl and a cationic conductane; 4) depolarisation can increase the Cl and cation conductance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the secretagogue-induced conductances were increased to a variable degree by depolarization.
calcium and secretagogue-induced conductances are present in acinar cells and that the secretory process is not mediated by a K conductance.
the electrical properties of the pancreatic acinar cells are not the same as those of the pancreatic ductal cells.
